lines.text: THE DOCTOR, FATHER OF BOTH CHINAS

lines.para: Sun Yat-sen died in 1925, before the civil war. So he never had to choose between the Communists and the Nationalists. Both camps claim him.
In Taipei, he is the “Father of the Nation”. His portrait dominates official halls, his face is on the hundred-dollar note, and a great memorial is dedicated to him.
In Beijing, he is the “forerunner of the revolution”. Every 1 October, his portrait is set up in Tiananmen Square, facing Mao’s.
His own family is split in two: his widow, Soong Ching-ling, becomes vice-president of the People’s Republic; his sister-in-law, Soong Mei-ling, is the wife of Chiang Kai-shek in Taiwan.
For a foreigner, having been the Doctor’s trusted man was worth a passport on both sides of the strait.
